gallup_2025.title: Obesity Rate Declining in U.S.
quotes: After peaking at a record high of 39.9% in 2022, the U.S. adult obesity rate has gradually declined to 37.0% in 2025.
combined data from three nationally representative surveys of 16,946 U.S. adults
interviewed by web in the first three quarters of 2025
Gallup uses respondents’ self-reported height and weight to calculate body mass index (BMI) and subsequent weight classes.
A “vanity effect” in how respondents present themselves may explain why Gallup’s obesity estimates are typically somewhat lower
The rate among men has dropped 2.3 percentage points to 35.2% in 2025,
while women's rate has dropped 3.5 points to 38.8%.

fourman_2025.authors: Fourman LT, Awwad A, Gutiérrez-Sacristán A, Dash CA, Johnson JE, Thistle AK, Chahal N, Stockman SL, Toribio M, Anekwe C, Gattu AK, Grinspoon SK
fourman_2025.title: Implications of a New Obesity Definition Among the All of Us Cohort
sample_notes: not weighted to the US population (an unweighted volunteer cohort); 61.0% female; Black or African American participants somewhat overrepresented (the paper)
the BMI-based 42.9% used race-specific BMI cut-offs per World Health Organization criteria

alroub_2025.authors: Al-Roub NM, Malik D, Essa M, Lu Y, Yang H, Spatz ES, Krumholz HM, Faridi KF
alroub_2025.title: Body Mass Index and Anthropometric Criteria to Assess Obesity
quotes: The study included 14 414 participants representing 237 700 000 US adults.
Survey-weighted obesity prevalence was 75.2% (95% CI, 73.8%-76.5%) overall.
39.9% (95% CI, 38.0%-41.0%) of all adults had BMI of 30 or greater.
A waist-to-height ratio >0.5 was considered a criterion for obesity in the primary analysis.
The most common abnormal anthropometric criterion was WHtR above 0.50 (80.0% [95% CI, 78.6%-81.3%] of adults)
Prevalence did not change from 2017-2020 to 2021-2023.
With a waist-to-height ratio cut-off above 0.6 instead of 0.5 (the alternative analysis), obesity prevalence was 58.4% (95% CI, 56.7%-60.2%).
Excess adiposity should be confirmed by either direct measurement of body fat, where available,
or at least one anthropometric criterion (eg, waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, or waist-to-height ratio)
At least two anthropometric criteria (waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio or waist-to-height ratio) regardless of BMI
In people with very high BMI (ie, >40 kg/m²), however, excess adiposity can pragmatically be assumed
Validated methods and age- gender- and ethnicity-appropriate cut-off points should be used for all anthropometric criteria.
21 states, Guam, and Puerto Rico had an obesity prevalence between 35% and less than 40%.
No state or territory had an obesity prevalence of 40% or higher.
all had an obesity prevalence higher than 25%, except the District of Columbia (24.2%).
